newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST-Taiwan May CPI seen rising 1.33 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Taiwan May CPI seen rising 1.33 pct yr/yr.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists forecast on Tuesday that the island's consumer price index will have risen a year-on-year 1.33 percent in May, well above April's actual 0.51 percent annual rise.
Official figures for May were scheduled to be issued at 0300 GMT on June 5 by the cabinet's Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics.
April's CPI growth was 0.51 percent year-on-year.

Economists said May's consumer prices in general should remain stable, though some cyclical rises were expected.
"Garment prices may continue to rise as the discount season for winter garment had ended," said HSBC James Capel analyst Stephen Wang.

Economists said they expected slightly higher food prices in May as the local price of pork, which fell sharply in late March and April due to an outbreak of hog mouth-and-foot disease, had largely recovered in May.
In the first four months of 1997, Taiwan's CPI grew 1.41 percent year-on-year, state statisticians said.
The cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development has set a 1997 CPI growth target of 3.0 percent.
In March, the central bank revised its forecast for 1997 CPI growth to around 3.0 percent from 3.31 percent.
